quest.title: Apocalypse
quest.description: The prophecy shall inevitably come to fruition, and the plans are all in place. All that's left... is to judge a god.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Primogem x30, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, that's Furina, right over there! She really is here all on her own...

choices.text: Shh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Mm-hmm.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Should I just give up? This is all... meaningless...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What was meant to happen did happen after all. Everyone's dead...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I'm sorry... I'm so sorry...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Give up, Furina. There's no point in holding out...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I'm sorry...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...But what can I even do, other than to repeat meaningless apologies over and over...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Furina...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah...! Who!? Who's that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, Furina. It's just us...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ahem... Heh... Ahahaha... So it is you, Blond Traveler from another land! Why, I almost thought you were someone from that mob of my ignorant subjects, come to kneel and beg for my forgiveness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Furina... You were crying just now, weren't you? The tear stains on your face are obvious...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Uh... What do you mean, tear stains? Oh, I remember. The show at the opera house earlier this morning was so moving, I'm still trying to process it.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hmph. Who did that uncivilized rabble think they were, disturbing my enjoyment of the arts?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: They even dared to doubt their Archon... I must teach them a lesson. Hehe, I can just imagine their twisted and frustrated faces once they realize that I'm nowhere to be found...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh! And I'm sure Neuvillette and those people from the Marechaussee Phantom are freaking out right next to them, too. Hehehe...

choices.text: Stop trying to act tough, Furina.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I... Of course not...

response.speaker: Unknown Voice Shouting
response.text: Hey, there she is! The Hydro Archon's over there!

response.speaker: Unknown Voice Shouting
response.text: Quick! After her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Furina, those people seem to be after you...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Th—They are? Hah, they're just some rabid fans who want to cut the line because they haven't been able to meet me in person, aren't they?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Tsk, tsk, that's against the rules! I can't let them get their way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh! Furina just ran off!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Quick, we have to catch up with her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...This should be the place, right? Hey! Furina!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a good hiding spot over here. Quick, come to Paimon before the rest of them catch up to you!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ahh... Wh—What? What is this place...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hurry! They're almost here!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Fine, fine, I suppose haste is warranted. Lead the way!

choices.text: You're actually beyond devastated right now, aren't you?
Stay quiet for now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *panting* Phew... Paimon's exhausted...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *panting* Phew... I'm so tired... I totally thought they had caught me...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ah, no, I mean, I nearly gave in to the sheer enthusiasm they displayed... Hahaha...

choices.text: This place is not what I'd call soundproof.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah... you're right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, that's a good girl.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huuuuuuuuuuuuh!?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What's happening? The ground's shaking... Is it an earthquake?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Another disaster just struck, I suspect.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, a quake of this kind preceded the flooding in Poisson, didn't it?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: It can't be... It's happening again...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, there's no need to worry too much about that! Neuvillette's made some emergency plans, so the evacuation should go a lot smoother this time.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Yeah... I hope you're right.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But the people of Poisson... They've already...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Has Furina finally reached her limit? Now that she's talking about her actual feelings, she's starting to look far less stiff...)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You begin to talk amongst yourselves as Furina slowly calms down...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...It's true. I've been investigating the prophecy for hundreds of years.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I once had informants all over Teyvat, searching for clues and feeding information back to me.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I've tried all kinds of ways, too, to hold back the sea. Anything to keep the coastline from advancing...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But all my efforts proved to be futile in the end. Really, the truth has been clear to me for a very long time...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: We cannot make an enemy of the divine. No matter what we do, the will of the Heavenly Principles will have its way, and the prophecy shall be fulfilled...

choices.text: But even then...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Give up? Ahh... I do love the sound of that phrase. It would mean finally coming to terms with fate, but also... for me to finally be free.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But that would also mean that all hope would disappear.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Indeed... I've thought about giving up so many times. Especially after we almost lost Poisson...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Fate is really unreasonable, isn't it? It has no heart, and obeys no rules. The prophecy has only just started to come true, and so many people have already lost their lives...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But just now... It all became clear to me. I still don't have the right to come to terms with fate on behalf of everyone else...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: As long as the final moment hasn't come, it's still not too late...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Don't worry. I... I will keep hope alive for everyone until the very end.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well! That's enough for now. I got the impulse to play the stricken maiden, but honestly, considering my rank and station, that wasn't a good fit at all, hehehe...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Don't take any of what I just said seriously! How could I possibly let Fontaine fall to the whims of trivial prophecy?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, Paimon could've sworn you were actually being honest just now...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We're running out of time... We can't just go back to square one like this. I have to get more information out of her...)

choices.text: Furina...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Although I don't know what you might be keeping from everyone...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Share my burden...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: That's impossible. It was fated, right from the start, that this would be my duty alone.

choices.text: But even if your burden doesn't need to be shared...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just share it with me. I'm what you'd call a "witness."

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: A witness... Ah, yes. I've heard that you came to Teyvat from beyond the stars, yes? In other words, you never belonged here...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: And if Teyvat is, in its entirety, a show on a stage, then you're just a "spectator," aren't you?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If that's the case...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (There's no time left... Please, Furina, just spit it out!)

choices.text: You can still choose to confide in someone.
Furina... You might not have to shoulder this burden alone.
You still haven't given up, right?
You might want to lower your voice to stay hidden.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ladies and gentlemen... this concludes my opening performance.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Now, without further ado... we may proceed to the trial of our god.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ah, so this is what it is. Yes... You deserve praise for the effort you took to raise the dramatic stakes.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Do not forget, however, that I am Focalors, the God of Justice — the embodiment of justice itself. Does it not strike you as even the least bit absurd to bring the very concept of justice to trial?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: May I interpret these words... as your refusal to stand trial?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In that case, you will have the opportunity to defend your honor through a duel.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You... You would draw your blade against a god?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I see... It seems like you have made up your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe it... She... She just surrendered!?

dialogues.speaker: Surprised Audience Member
dialogues.text: What the heck is going on? Did I just see an Archon surrender to a human?

dialogues.speaker: Dissatisfied Audience Member
dialogues.text: Wow, how utterly humiliating...

dialogues.speaker: Puzzled Audience Member
dialogues.text: Lady Furina, what is the meaning of this?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Shh!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It would seem that there has been a misunderstanding. To be clear, the raising of both hands is not always an indication of surrender...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looking for excuses again, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...I raised my hands just now to indicate my acceptance of the trial. No duel shall be necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I will admit that I've been running away for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, everyone. I was unable to protect the people of Poisson... It is my duty to stand trial for my crimes.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You are not the only ones to be disappointed in me. I, too, am exceedingly disappointed in myself.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Whew... But now, it is time for the Hydro Archon to show you her courage and resolve!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I, Furina, will use this trial to show the world the true meaning of justice!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (This time... I will protect you.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Applaud and rejoice! One of the most outrageous and fantastical arcs known to the Opera Epiclese is now unfolding before your eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Mark my words — this shall be one of the most exhilarating and brilliant shows ever to grace the stage of Fontaine! The trial of the Hydro Archon, Focalors, will now begin!

dialogues.speaker: Excited Audience Member
dialogues.text: Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Overexcited Audience Member
dialogues.text: Oh, now we're making history!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why does it feel like Furina just took over the whole thing... Like c'mon, didn't she just get forced to stand trial for her crimes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, even though she's still acting super dramatic, she is taking this seriously this time, right?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright, then... Who will be my opponent in this trial?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The court asks the prosecutor to please take the stand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Your Honor.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Is that so... Very well. Then please speak, witness of Teyvat, my accuser and fated opponent.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We were so close to getting her to tell us the truth... And it still turned out like this in the end.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's okay, though. As long as we can defeat Furina in court, we'll still have a chance to figure everything out.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Also, please allow me to ask, as the final question before the trial begins...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Just how much work did you do to force me onto this stage?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... We did do a lot of prep after the meeting that day...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I can go over the tasks assigned to the Spina di Rosula, since they were rather straightforward and easy.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Navia, the President of the Spina di Rosula...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Most of the people who participated in the disturbance this morning were my subordinates.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: They changed into plain clothes, and came to the opera house as regular audience members, waiting for the perfect opportunity to incite insurrection against you.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The people's resentment against their Archon has been building as more and more of the prophecy is fulfilled. A spark was all we needed to turn smoldering anger into a flame.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Moreover, according to our understanding and analysis of you, when something like that occurred, you would likely flee the scene and head to Poisson by yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So, we arranged for a second group to lie in wait there...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So, you mean... The ones who scoured the settlement for me were also from the Spina...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And their goal was to force you to step into the Giant Magic Box, so you may personally participate in the greatest magic performance in all of Fontainian history.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: That's right. That house was a magic box, rather than someone's residence.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: As the "Super Ultimate" version of the setup that I used when I first performed at the Opera Epiclese...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The volume of the box was increased by a whole order of magnitude, and the distance it traversed was the entire gap between Poisson and Erinnyes. Its cargo, of course...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Was an Archon, instead of a human.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: My thanks, Furina. Without your help, we could never have pulled off such an extraordinary performance.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Uh... You're welcome?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Of course, this performance was only made possible with "Father"'s support. The House of the Hearth spent a massive amount of labor and Mora to pull this off...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We had to select a location, construct the Giant Magic Box, dig a tunnel, and open up a path through the water... It was a lot of work for all of us.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So, in other words... the "earthquake" that we felt within the Giant Magic Box was just a normal tremor from the transportation of the whole house?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right. It wasn't a sign of another disaster to come.

choices.text: Sorry about that.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hmph, then... I can guess Neuvillette and Clorinde's parts.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: You gathered a crowd, prepared a stage, and made sure that the Champion Duelist would be immediately ready for a fight...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: All so that as soon as I appeared on the stage, the trial may commence without a hitch. Am I right?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Yes, that is correct.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well, Clorinde, I must commend you for your courage. Only the most outstanding Champion Duelist in all of Fontaine would accept a duel with an Archon without flinching.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: #As for you, {NICKNAME}... I suppose your role was to keep me distracted with conversation once you found me in Poisson.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: You'd make sure that I didn't notice anything amiss, before revealing yourself as my prosecutor once we'd arrived onto the stage...

choices.text: No.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh?

choices.text: My mission...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We hoped that you'd share your secret with us...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hehehe, is that so? Then I suppose I must have missed my final chance...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: It's fine, it matters not. What's done is done...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: The stage is already set, so there's no reason to disappoint the audience. Let's see this trial through to the very end!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Yeah... The only thing we can do now is to judge the Hydro Archon.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Still, I can't help but be a little bothered by that conversation earlier. What did Furina want to say to me right before we arrived on the stage...?)

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: #{F#Madam}{M#Sir} Prosecutor, please allow me to pass this along...

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: This is a document that Miss Charlotte applied for and received permission to share with you during the trial. According to her, it should speed up the proceedings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Charlotte wanted to give us something? Ooh, so she's here too. Hey, Charlotte!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see... Isn't this the "exclusive interview" that she did with us before? So she's already finished it, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, then that means this document is a perfect timeline of everything that's happened ever since we stepped foot in Fontaine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So in other words... we can refer to this "anthology of evidence" every time we want to use something from our journey as evidence for an argument!

choices.text: It's a super practical gift.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's quickly confirm the information in it... Just think of it as a refresher, alright?

choices.text: I never would have thought of using it this way.
Was to give you one last chance.
You guessed wrong.
We deceived you back there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It has been established that all Fontainians can dissolve in water from the Primordial Sea. And that means...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Since you insist on claiming to be a god and not a human, then there's a method that you can use right here and now to eliminate all suspicions of you being the latter.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Miss Navia, please apply to serve as a temporary attorney for the prosecution before addressing the court. Though you act in partnership with the prosecutor, you must still adhere to proper procedure.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Super sorry, Monsieur Chief Justice. I swear this really will be the last time that I'll speak out of turn.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Now, I've brought some seawater from Poisson. As everyone knows, a massive flood struck the area not long ago, taking many lives...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Including those of some of my closest friends.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So, Miss Furina, would you dare to touch some of this seawater?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: If we are to believe that you are indeed the real Hydro Archon, touching this seawater would have no effect on you. All it should do is strengthen your case.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But if you don't dare to touch it, then we would have basically proved the reverse.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, and I must remind you that after the disaster at Poisson, nobody wants to see any more people dissolve.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I do hope you'll act prudently, and choose the simpler path of admitting guilt.

dialogues.speaker: Agreeing Audience Member
dialogues.text: Navia from the Spina di Rosula... The Spina has governed Poisson for many years... I guess her suggestion is valid.

dialogues.speaker: Pondering Audience Member
dialogues.text: If Lady Furina is indeed just a human, she's probably a Fontainian like all the rest of us. Would she really dare to try...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh... Furina?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Lady Furina, this "test" has been unilaterally proposed by the prosecution. As it falls outside the realm of standard court proceedings, you possess the right to decline participation.

dialogues.speaker: Conscientious Audience Member
dialogues.text: Well, of course he had to tell her that, but refusing to participate is basically the same as a confession of guilt.

dialogues.speaker: Worried Audience Member
dialogues.text: She's just staring at the water without saying a single word... It really does seem like she's quite terrified of it. That could only mean...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (What's going on? Is she really planning to... That's not what we thought she would...)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *inhale*... *exhale*...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Due to the inherent risk of the test, Lady Furina, you may—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaaaaah!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She actually...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *pant*... *pant*... Ahh...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I... I'm fine! Look! Look at me, everyone. My hand is still here. I haven't been dissolved!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Will you believe me now? I really am your Archon. I'm nothing like a normal human, who would fall apart as soon as they touch this water. Really, was this not the most obvious thing in the world?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Miss Sigewinne? If you are present, Miss Sigewinne, please come forward and attend to the defendant.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Sige...winne?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Don't be nervous, it'll just take a few seconds... Hmm, let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, that should be enough.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please announce the results of your evaluation to the court, Miss Sigewinne.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: As everyone doubtlessly saw, Miss Furina was displaying symptoms of hyperventilation and flushed skin. These indicate that...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: She was experiencing the adverse effects of exposure to Primordial Seawater. The extent to which she was affected is the same as other humans when exposed to Primordial Seawater of a similar concentration.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Thank you, Miss Sigewinne. Lady Furina, you may return to the defendant's stand.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Wait. What did she just say? I didn't get dissolved! Shouldn't that be enough to prove my innocence?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, considering your tendency to run from your problems, we did originally prepare a direct sample of the seawater around Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: However, after extensive discussion, we exchanged it for a sample that is not concentrated enough to dissolve an actual human. After all, on the off chance that something entirely unexpected might occur...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We don't want anyone else to lose their life to the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, so out of regard for Furina's life, you secured a low concentration sample, and asked the head nurse to serve as an expert witness...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a great thing that the direct sample wasn't actually used. Furina could have...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I... I can't believe... You...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But what's really going on here? Furina can't have not known the consequences of touching that water as a human...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is too unlike how she usually acts... Unless... It's actually more important for her to keep up her facade than to save her own life!?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But... hadn't she given up on everything a long time ago?)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Listen to me, listen to me, everyone... Please don't give me such cold and disdainful looks. What happened just now didn't prove a single thing!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Think about it. How can you conclusively prove that an Archon can't also be affected by the Primordial Seawater?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Also, also! If I was really just a human, why would I dare to just put my hand in that kind of water!?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Please, everyone, anyone, just listen to me. I swear, I really am your Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Exasperated Audience Member
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Exasperated Audience Member
dialogues.text: ...I don't think anything she says at this point will sway anyone. The odds are just too stacked against her now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: With all the things that have been said... Paimon doesn't think there's any way left for Furina to win.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I believe the time for argument and presentation of evidence has come to an end. If there are no objections, we will move on to the final judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In my capacity as Chief Justice, I shall now render judgment on Furina's misrepresentation of herself as the Archon of Fontaine. As a human who knowingly deceived her fellow citizens, Furina is—

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Guilty.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: We shall now turn to the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale to render the final verdict on the charges.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: According to the judgment of the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, Furina is—

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's wrong? What's the Oratrice's verdict?

choices.text: It can't be...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...No, the Oratrice also displays a guilty verdict.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't that correct, then?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: However, the exact wording of the verdict is thus. "The Hydro Archon, guilty"...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: "To be punished via the death sentence."

response.speaker: Astonished Audience Member
response.text: The... The death sentence!?

response.speaker: Doubtful Audience Member
response.text: That's actually one of the available sentences!? I've always thought that it was just a myth...

response.speaker: Emotional Audience Member
response.text: The one and only time the death sentence has been handed out at the court, and it's been given to the very person we've worshipped as the God of Justice? What an unexpected twist...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Furina's been sentenced to death by the Oratrice!? We just wanted to use the trial to show her the seriousness of things, so she'd tell us the truth... How did things escalate this quickly!?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: This outcome is indeed quite strange. According to Fontaine's current definitions of justice, as well as its recommendations for criminal sentences...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Is this sentence really appropriate for the crimes that have been committed...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, even Vacher wasn't sentenced to death by the Oratrice... You know, the real evil mastermind behind the serial disappearances case.

choices.text: What's more strange is...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Indeed. Not only is Furina's sentence overly excessive, the very point of our trial today was also to prove that Furina has never been the Hydro Archon in the first place.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: But now, the Oratrice seems to have deliberately invoked the title of the "Hydro Archon." What does this mean?

choices.text: Instead of Furina, the Oratrice rendered judgment on "the Hydro Archon."
Did the Oratrice just declare Furina to be innocent?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Err... Excuse me... If I may interrupt...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Is... the trial still going?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Freminet! You finally made it. I assume this means you've completed your mission?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Mhm. Any mission "Father" assigns to me will always be top priority.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With some help from the other Fatui, Freminet brings a stone slate onto the stage...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that the first prophecy slate?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so The Knave privately arranged for Freminet to try and find the missing slate.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I looked everywhere, and finally found it at the bottom of the sea. It took me a long time to get around some dangerous stretches of water...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: But... has the trial already concluded? Then... Doesn't that mean I've come too late? Oh no, "Father" will be disappointed in me...

choices.text: Don't worry, the mystery hasn't been resolved yet.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Thank you for your hard work, Mr. Freminet. Please allow me to review the record left on the slate.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I believe that you have also already seen the other existing slates. I would like you to also come here and confirm their contents.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... So what do you see? What is it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This looks like...

choices.text: The previous Hydro Archon releasing her divine power...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I believe I have now made sense of the Hydro Archon's crime. It has to do with Fontaine's lost history.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Isn't the Hydro Archon just guilty of deceiving her people... Wait, no, that's Furina, and we've already proven that she's not the Hydro Archon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So when you say "Hydro Archon," do you mean the real Hydro Archon we've been kind of talking about?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: In truth, everything that you've encountered in Fontaine up until this point can be traced back to the contents of these stone slates.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: However, I am uncertain as to how much sense they currently make to you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: An association between the contents of the slates and the events in real life...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, let's try to recall the contents of the other three stone slates... Paimon will do her best to help you remember!

choices.text: Turning the Oceanids into... human beings.
It's still not too late for you to shine.

talks.objective: Discover the connection between the events in real life and the slates

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, oh, Paimon gets it now... So that's how you can make sense of it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But then it feels like... We're going to have to share some truly shocking revelations.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Let's hear them.

choices.text: The first slate reveals that...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Incredible. Lyney, did you hear that?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We're... not real humans?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All Fontainians were originally created by the late previous Hydro Archon, with Oceanids as their basis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The evidence for that can be found in... How only Fontainians could dissolve in Primordial Seawater, and how all the girls Vacher dissolved were also turned into Oceanids...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and according to Navia, when she was about to get dissolved, she also saw everyone gathered around for a trial, all of them in the shape of Oceanids...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Indeed.

choices.text: The second slate reveals that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and it follows from the content of the first slate that she probably angered Celestia by creating humans without prior permission.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That could also explain why the Oratrice judged the Hydro Archon to be guilty — it's to account for that ancient "sin."

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: The Hydro Archon's true sin... was creating us?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: And yet, after many hundreds of years, the Hydro Archon's creations have turned around to try to judge the Archon within the Opera Epiclese. The twists of history are often the most unexpected of all.

choices.text: As for the third slate...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, isn't the image here just like when Navia fell into the sea?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, wouldn't it be trying to show the image of the Hydro Archon also falling into the sea once the prophecy has been fulfilled in the fourth slate?

choices.text: The fourth slate...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In the end, the people will all be dissolved into the waters, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne... Only then will the sins of the people of Fontaine be washed away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did Paimon get all that right?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: You've made some keen deductions. I must say, given how much you still don't know, it is impressive that you've already managed to connect so many pieces of the truth.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: However... While you were able to decode all the information on the slates, they had also been etched with an additional layer of hidden information using a different power source.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: When we were at the ruins, I tried to decipher the hidden information recorded in the slates. But since we only had three slates at the time, I was unable to come to a full conclusion.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Now that the slate collection is complete, I shall make another attempt to decipher the narrative recorded within. If everything goes well, we should finally be informed of the unadulterated truth.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Well? Did you get it?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I believe I should share this truth not only with you, but with all the people of Fontaine as well. I will try to briefly summarize it for you...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Your hypotheses regarding the origin of Fontainians and the sin of the Hydro Archon were both correct.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: In the Fontaine of old, the previous Hydro Archon sensed the yearning of her Oceanid familiars for life on land.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: The Oceanids were enamored with the beauty and romanticism of human beings, and wishing to have those experiences for themselves, expressed to the Hydro Archon their desire to become of a similar kind.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: However, even though water as an element is intricately linked with the power of life, the Hydro Archon, as one of The Seven, did not possess the authority to create a new form of human life.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Not one to give in, she eventually found a way to create permanent humanoid bodies for her familiars by appropriating the power of this planet's Primordial Sea.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: She poured Primordial Seawater into the Oceanids' blood vessels, creating humanoid mimics in the process.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: But if Fontainians were to ever come into direct contact with Water from the Primordial Sea, the power within their bodies would escape these artificial restraints and return to the Sea. As a result, their forms would collapse, and they would be reverted to their original forms as Oceanids.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Of course, the Hydro Archon never received permission from the Heavenly Principles to create a new "human" race...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: And thus, the Hydro Archon and all of her creations came to shoulder the original sin of "appropriating the power of the Primordial Sea."

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...That is the true history of how the people of Fontaine first came into being.

response.speaker: Bewildered Audience Member
response.text: So you... I... We were all Oceanids before we were turned into human beings?

response.speaker: Out-Of-Control Audience Member
response.text: That's way too much information for me... I think I'm just going to pretend that I never heard a single thing.

response.speaker: Dozy Audience Member
response.text: Wait, but if that's the truth, we can't let the Hydro Archon be sentenced to death! After all, her only sin was creating us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This really might be too much information for your regular Fontainian... But it does answer a lot of our questions.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Alas, your hypothesis regarding the third and fourth stone slates was inaccurate. The slates' respective positions are, in fact, correct.

choices.text: So, they are in the right order?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: A key point of the visual on the third slate is how all the individuals depicted in the water are humans, rather than Oceanids.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: They have not been dissolved, which implies that the water depicted in this slate is not water from the Primordial Sea.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: The nation of Fontaine is the nation of Hydro as well as the nation of trials and justice. Instead of being the literal element, the water in the scene symbolizes judgment and justice.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: You may also recall Navia's experience. When she fell into the sea, her consciousness was surrounded by that of many others, who intended to hold a trial to determine her fate.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Therefore, the meaning of the third slate is...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...That the people of Fontaine shall try the Hydro Archon at the court of justice.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Yes, it refers to our present situation.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I think I'm following now. So what you're saying is, even though we decided to put on this trial to avoid fulfilling the prophecy...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: In truth, everything we've done has happened exactly as the prophecy foretold... So now it seems we're the ones making sure it comes true...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What should we do?

choices.text: I don't know...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: No matter what, the prophecy will be fulfilled... Is this what it feels like to be a prisoner of fate?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If that's the case... Does that mean the scene in the fourth slate will also be fulfilled soon?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I would like to point out another small fallacy in your deductions.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: About the fourth slate — you probably thought that the eruption of Primordial Seawater beneath the Fortress of Meropide served as the surest sign that the prophecy was about to come to pass, yes?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: However, I believe that rather than being a sure sign, that eruption could in fact only be a small warning of something far worse to come.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: As for the root cause of the catastrophe... I believe you've already encountered it once before.

choices.text: I have?
Wait, could it be...
It... feels like there's no way out of this.
It can't be...
What is the third slate supposed to represent, then?
Depicts the fulfillment of the prophecy as it's already widely known.
I'm still convinced that it should come after the fourth slate.
The crime of the Hydro Archon... was her creation of Fontainians from Oceanids.
Fontainians are not real humans.

talks.objective: Find the source of the calamity in the prophecy slates

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: We didn't believe that such a crazy disaster could happen at first, did we? But after "that incident," it was just a question of "when," and not "if."

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Indeed, that greedy beast in the Primordial Sea is the true root cause of the catastrophe.

talks.objective: Discuss how to deal with the All-Devouring Narwhal

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was way too close! How did that thing just burst into the opera house!? Wait. Was that the huge whale you saw in your dream?

choices.text: That's right.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: So, we've met it at last... I understand very well why it has chosen to make an appearance here.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: That "whale" does not belong to Teyvat. It is a monster that has traversed the stars, weeping all the while.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: It has been greedily consuming the energy from the planet's Primordial Sea, using it to grow. That is the main cause for the rising sea levels...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: And once it has finished consuming all of the energy contained within the Sea, its next step will be...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: You said that when the Hydro Archon first created Fontainians out of Oceanids, she filled their blood vessels with Primordial Seawater...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Precisely. That whale finds the "blood" of Fontainians nigh impossible to resist.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Therefore, when it left the Primordial Sea, it decided to make its next stop a packed opera house full of food — food in the form of Fontainians.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We just barely managed to push it back, right? In that case... Won't it come back to target the people again once it's managed to recover its strength?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: That is correct. Indeed, it is more accurate to say that we should thank that Harbinger for buying us some time. Without him, the whale would have likely come onto land far sooner.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: From the way he looked, he must have been fighting the creature for quite a long time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That battle maniac... We've always known that he had a special connection with that whale, but we definitely didn't expect it to help us out like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, now that we know that this whale is the actual cause of the disaster recorded in the prophecy, all we need to do to stop the prophecy would be to find a way to beat it up, right?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: It is too late...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you mean?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: It had already absorbed too much of the Primordial Sea's energy before we could notice it. At this point, it has become practically integrated with the Sea itself.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Even if the entirety of Teyvat were to be destroyed, it could still survive, and swim off towards some other world.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That... That's not something I will accept.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We've already done everything we can, and we even found the true culprit...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We've come so far! You can't just tell me that the last hurdle is some impossible foe. That's just not fair.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Indeed. That's not how a grand performance should end.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I'll fight it to the end. No matter what.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So the prophecy will be fulfilled no matter what, huh...

response.speaker: Mage "N"
response.text: The prophecy... Yes, what has been prophesized will be fulfilled. You may view such things as "the history of the future."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (After everything, it still turned out like this... We couldn't fight against fate.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, but if this is all about fate...)

response.speaker: Mage "N"
response.text: Just as prophecies are usually only the future as seen from the perspectives of the gods, could things be happening in hidden corners where the gods' gaze does not fall?

response.speaker: Mage "N"
response.text: Ultimately, fate shall serve as your only guide no matter what will happen in Teyvat's future. All you need to do is to play your part.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Could it be... That even if the prophecy will be fulfilled, there will still be a way to save everyone?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Did I... miss something...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, I forgot about Furina! What was it that she wanted to say to me at that last moment, in the Giant Magic Box?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What is her real secret?)

choices.text: I'd wager that it's also the one that Childe saw when he was young.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The prosecution and the defense are both in position. The trial shall now begin.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Come on, Neuvillette. There's no need to repeat all the unimportant legalese.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Just fast forward to the part where the prosecution lays out my offenses. As the defendant, and the lead actress of this performance, I still haven't even been informed of my supposed guilt in all of this.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Of course, it is only natural for humans to struggle to understand the actions of a god. However, you will need more than that to convict me of a crime...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That is true, but my charge here is unrelated to your conduct as an Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Instead, I would like to charge you as a fraud who's never been the Archon in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Astonished Audience Member
dialogues.text: Wait... what was that? Lady Furina's a fraud?

dialogues.speaker: Doubtful Audience Member
dialogues.text: Hey... I came here thinking that we were going to try the Hydro Archon for forsaking her duty, but did I hear that right? She's not our Archon at all?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Charge accepted.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Lady Furina. Do you plead guilty to the charge?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Lady Furina?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I plead not guilty. How can I be guilty?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: There is no way that I, Focalors, otherwise known as Furina de Fontaine, a member of The Seven, and the Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws of Fontaine, could be anything other than your true Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Fair-Minded Audience Member
dialogues.text: Yeah... Even though Lady Furina can be rather eccentric, isn't it going too far to doubt her very identity?

dialogues.speaker: Suspicious Audience Member
dialogues.text: Yeah, I've never questioned her identity either. Sure, Lady Furina can be super irresponsible, but what grounds does that prosecutor have to make such a huge claim...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I have cause to believe that common sense will prevail in this case. Many of the members of the audience have known me as the Hydro Archon ever since they were born — there would be no fooling their memory.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: See? Even the Oratrice has decided to show me its favor. Are you sure you want to commit to a charge that will never be upheld?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: If you wish to drop the case, I can promise you, as the God of Justice, that you will not have to face trial for making a false accusation. We will treat everything that's happened as a dramatic spectacle, and move on with our lives. What do you say to that?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: An argument with near-impossible odds, huh? We have to not only refute Furina's claims, but also overturn the long-held beliefs of the people...

choices.text: The people only see you as their Archon...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well, I tried to give you the chance to surrender. If you must persist, then let me ask: If you believe I'm not the Archon, then what manner of being do you think I am?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: And if I was not the Archon, then how did I manage to live for over five hundred years?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I've got to think carefully... What do we know to be "special" about Furina, exactly?)

choices.text: Because that's their long-held belief.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: First of all, you may be a member of another long-lived race, which would allow you to naturally possess an extended lifespan. And second of all, even if that wasn't the case, there could be other ways to extend your life...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Such as... a curse.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmph... Who gave you that idea? Was it The Knave? You'd sink so low as to use a Harbinger's words against me?

choices.text: It doesn't matter who gave us the information.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: A curse... I once thought it possible that the aura of an Archon might naturally resemble a type of curse.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: But in light of this claim, perhaps what I sensed was not your divinity, but a curse after all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Neuvillette sensed it too, huh?

choices.text: So, Furina...

response.speaker: Surprised Audience Member
response.text: Lady Furina... is actually human?

response.speaker: Contemplative Audience Member
response.text: Well, it is true that it's extremely difficult to tell humans and gods apart just by looking at them. It's not impossible...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well, don't start celebrating too early now. Even if I have been carrying a curse like you said, how does that prove that I am merely a human being?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Besides, everyone knows that the main difference between a human and a god is the possession of "authority." Gods can do what humans cannot — that's why they're worshipped as gods.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: For centuries, manifestations of my authority have served the nation of Fontaine.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: One need only to turn their eyes towards the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale in this very opera house, or consider the Indemnitium that is used in every aspect of life.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait... That one trial proved the opposite. Furina actually has no control over the Oratrice at all...)

choices.text: Instead of an Archon, could you just be a cursed human?
What matters is the veracity of the claim.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that doesn't sound right. Paimon doesn't think this clue can be used as compelling evidence to build our case...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You tried to reference the Oratrice, but weren't you as confused as all the rest of us when the Oratrice declared Childe to be guilty without any proof? Otherwise, you should have come up with a good explanation for that by now...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Didn't I make myself clear at the time? The decisions of the gods are naturally difficult for humans to comprehend. There is no need to provide an explanation...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Lady Furina, I believe a reminder of your current circumstances is in order.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: While the court is in session, the principles of justice and the law must come before all else. While you are an Archon, you are also first and foremost the defendant in this trial.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: You will prove yourself unable to defend against the prosecution's charges if you continue to withhold vital information against the rules of the court.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I never thought... You'd use that kind of rhetoric against me...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: That was no trick of rhetoric, Lady Furina. I have merely reiterated the rules of the court, rules that all should respect and follow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you neither knew why Childe was declared guilty, nor did you understand the structure and operations of the Oratrice...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Instead of having been created by you, the "manifestations of authority" you mentioned have been made by the real Hydro Archon, haven't they?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The real Hydro Archon? Well, now you're really losing me.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It is true that I did not know why the Oratrice gave out a guilty verdict that day.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But the Oratrice handed out that verdict unilaterally, and it has been operating independently ever since it was first created.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You can't... You can't argue that just because a divine creation is flawed, that the god behind it must also be no god at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's still throwing out all kinds of excuses... Seems like she's confident that we won't be able to produce proof that she has no power over the Oratrice.

choices.text: Sure, we can put the Oratrice aside for now...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: My power as an Archon? There are many ordinary citizens in the audience. How can I just carelessly demonstrate the formidable power of an Archon...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: If that poses a concern, I'm prepared to extend my protection to the audience.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Erm... Y—You don't need to go that far...

choices.text: A brief demonstration of your power over Hydro should be quite harmless.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aren't you the Hydro Archon? Or is it that you can't even wield the power of Hydro, much less the authority of a god?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...Indemnitium, yes, it's all because of Indemnitium! All Archons derive their power from the faith of the people, and I've converted the people's faith in justice into Indemnitium.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Thus did I give up all of my divine power to provide everyone with energy for their daily lives. Have you ever seen a more magnanimous god?

response.speaker: Suspicious Audience Member
response.text: Isn't that... a huge stretch?

response.speaker: Retorting Audience Member
response.text: Yeah, no matter how generous an Archon can be, how could they give up all of their power? Can a god with no power even still be called a god?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It seems like nobody's buying Furina's excuse.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hey, come now, everyone... Please don't stare at me as if I was a liar...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I'm still the same Furina you knew, right? The one that you loved? Shouldn't you want to believe in me?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Please... You've got to believe me...

response.speaker: Serious Audience Member
response.text: If what the prosecutor said is true, she really has committed a grave offense...

response.speaker: Thinking Audience Member
response.text: Did she deceive all of us, and all of our parents and grandparents too? And all of our ancestors, ever since they were born?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Enough... That's enough...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Tell me, then...! If I'm not the real Hydro Archon, then who is?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If you have no evidence of another Hydro Archon's existence, nor can you find anyone who can back up their claim to be such, then what grounds have you to say that I'm not actually the real deal?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, she came up with yet another argument... Ugh, how can we refute her now? Seems like she really doesn't want to give up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (If we can't prove that she isn't the Archon, we can try to prove that she is just a human. And if she's only human...)

choices.text: Surely an Archon can at least match the capacities of a human with a Vision?
But then, Miss Furina, could you give us a brief demonstration of your power as an Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that doesn't sound right. Paimon doesn't think this clue can be used as compelling evidence to build our case...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that doesn't sound right. Paimon doesn't think this clue can be used as compelling evidence to build our case...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We know from the case of the serial disappearances of young women that Fontainians can be dissolved in Primordial seawater...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps what is about to take place has all happened before.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's not as simple as falling into the sea...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The prophecy from the stone slates found its way into society, but not many people believed it at first...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound quite right. Let's think about this some more...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They will dissolve into the waters of the Primordial Sea, and then they'll be like the Poisson residents Navia met when she fell into the sea... They'll turn into Oceanids.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The first stone slate describes what you had just said. It seems to show the previous Hydro Archon using her divine power, and then the Oceanids turn into humans...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that mean that Fontainians are transformed Oceanids? Paimon wasn't expecting that... But if Oceanids can turn into humans, then perhaps this process can be "reversed" as well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The second stone slate shows Celestia floating in the sky, and the Hydro Archon and her people worshiping it together... but the heavens still brought judgment down upon them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This must be the point when the Hydro Archon and the Fontainians were branded with their "original sin." Does this mean that the "original sin" and the "Hydro Archon's sin" are the same thing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The third slate shows the Hydro Archon sinking into the sea, surrounded by many people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that reminds Paimon, didn't we also watch that happen to someone else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, the fourth slate is the prophecy the Fontainians have been talking about. People dissolving into the sea, the Hydro Archon crying on her throne, and so on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't believe that such a crazy disaster could happen at first, did we? But after "that incident," it was just a question of "when," and not "if."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was both dream and reality.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The "Hydro Archon" was sentenced to death in court, shocking everyone present. Perhaps this means that her sin was actually Fontaine's "original sin"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Navia fell into the water inside those ruins, and she nearly dissolved. She was surrounded by the people of Poisson in a court within her consciousness, and was forced to take part in a trial meant to make her stay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The eruption of the Primordial Sea at the Fortress of Meropide was the surest sign that the prophecy was about to come to pass no matter what.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The stone slates' content can all be verified by recent events. If we combined what we know together, loads of truths should come to light...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And the first stone slate tells us that long ago, the Hydro Archon used her power to turn Oceanids into humans...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This might be the reason that Fontainians can dissolve...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The true "sin" of the Hydro Archon that Neuvillette mentioned...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And the "original sin" cast down on the people of Fontaine by Celestia, as recorded on the stone slates...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When Navia fell into the sea, her consciousness was subjected to judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The stone slates show the people gathered around the Hydro Archon in the sea... Could that be alluding to the same thing?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Fortress of Meropide was nearly flooded with Primordial Seawater, which we know can cause Fontainians to dissolve. It seems increasingly likely that the prophecy may come true.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If we hadn't dealt with it in time, things could have gone very badly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They'll dissolve into the Primordial Sea, but won't cease to exist... Their essence will flow in the seawater, converge... and take the form of an Oceanid.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The truth, the original sin, the trial... and the root cause of the disaster.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we're talking about a "true culprit," that could only be "that thing" inside the Primordial Sea, right?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: This eruption was just a small warning of the things to come. We must find the root cause of the disaster...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place looks deserted... Guess all the survivors must have evacuated already. All that's left here are signs of devastation...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could Furina really be here? Let's try to find her as soon as possible.
